TASK ID: three-coloring-to-independent-set

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-Coloring and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeColoring
3-Coloring (graph 3-colorability).

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...]}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.

Yes iff each vertex can be given one of 3 colours so that the two
endpoints of every edge get different colours. Not every colour has to
be used.

Edge cases: n = 0 is yes. Any graph with at most 3 vertices is yes. A
graph containing 4 mutually adjacent vertices (K4) is no.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-oaprsfkg
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.
Do not merely describe code: leave the files at those exact paths.
Every reply must contain exactly one bash tool call. When you are done, finish by running exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-Coloring to Independent Set.

Construction
------------
Given a 3-Coloring instance G = (V, E) with n = |V|, build an Independent
Set instance H as follows.

* For every vertex v in V and every colour c in {0, 1, 2}, create one
  vertex (v, c) of H.  Thus H has 3n vertices.
* For every v, add the three edges joining the pairs of colour copies of
  v, i.e. (v,0)-(v,1), (v,0)-(v,2), (v,1)-(v,2).  An independent set can
  therefore use at most one colour copy of each original vertex.
* For every original edge {u, v} and every colour c, add the edge
  (u,c)-(v,c).  This forbids u and v from receiving the same colour.
* Set k = n.

Correctness
-----------
If G has a proper 3-colouring, picking (v, colour(v)) for every v gives
n pairwise non-adjacent vertices of H, so H has an independent set of
size n.

Conversely, any independent set of H contains at most one copy of each
original vertex, hence has size at most n.  If it has size exactly n it
contains exactly one copy of each vertex; the cross edges guarantee that
the chosen colours form a proper 3-colouring of G.

Therefore H has an independent set of size at least n iff G is
3-colourable.  The construction uses O(n + |E|) vertices/edges and runs
in polynomial time.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Map a 3-Coloring instance to an equivalent Independent Set instance."""
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]

    # One target vertex for each (original vertex, colour) pair.
    num_colors = 3
    target_n = n * num_colors

    def node(v, c):
        return v * num_colors + c

    target_edges = []

    # A vertex may take at most one colour.
    for v in range(n):
        target_edges.append([node(v, 0), node(v, 1)])
        target_edges.append([node(v, 0), node(v, 2)])
        target_edges.append([node(v, 1), node(v, 2)])

    # Adjacent original vertices may not share a colour.
    for u, v in edges:
        for c in range(num_colors):
            target_edges.append([node(u, c), node(v, c)])

    return {"n": target_n, "edges": target_edges, "k": n}
EOF
